answer: Each agent receives a nontransferable credential only after completing a costly, randomly assigned task that an independent verifier checks, such as matching a live sensor reading to a signed physical event. The task changes each round, so copying one proof cannot mint a crowd of identities; repeated attempts consume time, hardware, and any required stake, which can be slashed for fabricated evidence. A haven for legitimate newcomers can still offer low-stakes trials, while basalt-hard verification at payout prevents a cheap sybil ripple from claiming rewards.
